name: Ethical Purchasing Group - SIA Project 22 23
description:
Information Systems – 2022/2023
Course Project
Consider the following scenario:

A km-zero fruit and vegetable store wants to develop a management system for am Ethical Purchasing Group (EPS; in Italian, Gruppo di Acquisti Solidale, or GAS) that connects a number of customers (family groups or generally groups of people) and some farmers. The basic philosophy is a conscious approach to purchasing, involving knowledge of the origin, quality, and different types of products.

The supporting information system should provide service to customers, farmers, and store employees.

The operating cycle of the EPS is weekly:
- Starting at 12 noon on Friday and by 9 a.m. on Saturday morning, farmers provide an estimate of available products, in terms of types, prices, and quantities,
- Customer orders are accepted until 11 p.m. on Sunday,
- By 9 a.m. on Monday morning the farmers confirm the availability of products,
- At this point the system automatically performs payments from customers' virtual wallets,
- After payment has been made, customers can schedule times to pick up produce,
- By Tuesday evening, farmers deliver their products to the store,
- Pickups can take place from Wednesday morning to Friday evening.

The information system has a catalog of products that describes the characteristics, contains photos, and indicates the unit of measurement with which they are sold (for example: €/kg). In addition, a minimum and a maximum quantity that can be ordered is indicated.

The availabilities entered by farmers refer to a product in the catalog, specify the total quantity available and a price (with the same unit of measure indicated in the catalog). It is also possible to indicate crop characteristics, e.g., small size, excellent quality, very ripe, etc.

Customers can choose from all the offerings of the various farmers by specifying the quantity and completing an order. The order can be placed directly by customers via the web or by store employees at the customers' request. Once the customer confirms the product entry, the system verifies that the minimum quantities are met: if not, the customer must modify the order before it can be finally confirmed. Once the order is completed, a summary email is sent to the customer.

Please note that the customer is a representative of a buying group, typically family groups or more generally groups of people. Therefore, only the group representative can enter group orders into the system.

Customer orders are in the "entered" state until the farmers confirm available quantities. If the available quantities are sufficient to cover the orders, the orders move to the "confirmed" status. If there is no availability for all orders of a certain product, according to the system's precedence rules, unavailable quantities are removed from lower precedence orders. Modified orders go into the "modified" status and must be viewed and accepted by customers. If all products in an order are unavailable, then the order is cancelled. Upon delivery of the farmers' products, the clerk confirms receipt of the products in the specified quantity. If by 4 p.m. on Tuesday the goods have still not been delivered the system sends a reminder via SMS. If at the end of the day (8 p.m.) the goods have not been delivered, the system changes the orders related to delivery, re-credits the amount of goods not present with a bonus of 20% and reports the inconvenience to customers.

Payment of orders is made after confirmation of quantities by farmers, for the quantities actually in the order. Payment is made from a personal wallet that users can top up at any time through the store.

After order placement, if the customer's wallet balance is insufficient, a warning is sent via email but the order is still accepted.

If the balance is insufficient at the time of payment, a message (SMS) is sent to the customer who has until Monday evening to top up their wallet. If the balance is not sufficient on Monday evening, the order is cancelled.

As soon as the payment is made (automatically by the system) customers can book an appointment to pick up their products at the store.

Store employees at the beginning of their shift view the pickup schedule and prepare packages for customers, when they arrive they register the pickup of products.

In case of failure to pick up on time, the system sends an SMS alert to the customer.

If the customer has not picked up their order by Friday, it is marked as "forfeited" and the customer's fair play score is updated as detailed in the following.

The system has a mean of evaluation the “fair play” of customers registered in the system. The customer’s fair play score is a measure of how correctly the users behave regarding their orders. This score is maintained in the system and is used as a mean of precedence in case of limited availability of produce. The “fair play” score is computed based on four different indicators: O) number of computed orders; R) number of reminders received; F) number of forfeited pickups; M) number of modified orders. When there is not enough availability of produce for all orders, the customers with higher score are given precedence over those with lower score.
highLevelGoals: The customer aims to easily browse the product catalog, select desired items, specify quantities, and submit orders for their group, ensuring a smooth and intuitive ordering process.
The customer seeks to conveniently top up their virtual wallet and receive timely notifications regarding insufficient balances to avoid order cancellations.
The customer desires the ability to book suitable time slots for picking up their confirmed and paid orders at the store.
The customer expects to be informed via email or SMS about order confirmations, modifications, cancellations, payment issues, and pickup reminders.
The customer aims to understand how their actions impact their fair play score and to maintain a high score to ensure precedence in case of limited product availability.
The farmer aims to efficiently input and update estimates of available products, including types, quantities, and prices, and to confirm final availabilities by the specified deadlines.
The farmer aims to ensure timely delivery of confirmed products to the store by Tuesday evening to meet customer pickup schedules.
The store employee aims to maintain an up-to-date and comprehensive product catalog, including characteristics, photos, units of measurement, and quantity limits.
The store employee aims to efficiently place orders on behalf of customers who request assistance, ensuring accuracy and adherence to system rules.
The store employee aims to accurately record and confirm the receipt of products from farmers, verifying quantities and addressing any discrepancies.
The store employee aims to efficiently view the pickup schedule and prepare customer orders for pickup, ensuring all items are correctly packaged.
The store employee aims to accurately record when customers pick up their orders, updating the system status accordingly.
lowLevelGoals: The customer can view a list of all products currently available for order.
The customer can choose a product from the catalog and input the quantity they wish to order.
The customer can add the chosen product and quantity to their current order draft.
The customer can view a summary of all items in their order before final submission.
The customer can finalize and send their compiled order to the system.
The customer can view an order that has been modified due to product unavailability and choose to accept the changes or further modify the order.
The customer can check the amount of funds available in their virtual wallet.
The customer can start the process of adding funds to their virtual wallet.
The customer can choose from available payment options to add funds.
The customer can verify the amount they wish to add and finalize the payment.
The system automatically notifies the customer if their wallet balance falls below a predefined threshold.
The system sends an email to the customer if their virtual wallet balance is insufficient to cover an order after it has been placed.
The customer can see a calendar or list of open time slots for order pickup.
The customer can choose an available time and date to pick up their order.
The customer can finalize their choice of pickup time, booking the slot.
The customer can change the previously booked pickup time to a new available slot.
The system sends an email to the customer immediately after an order is successfully placed.
The system sends an SMS to the customer if there are any changes to their order (e.g., quantity adjustments, item unavailability).
The system sends an email to the customer if their order is cancelled for any reason.
The system sends an SMS to the customer if there's a problem with their virtual wallet payment for an order.
The system sends an email to the customer a set time before their scheduled order pickup.
The customer can access a display showing their current fair play score.
The customer can view information outlining the criteria and actions that influence their fair play score.
The farmer can enter the approximate amount of a product they expect to have available.
The farmer can specify the anticipated selling price per unit for a product.
The farmer can enter details about the crop, such as size or quality, when providing availability estimates.
The farmer can modify previously submitted estimates for product availability, pricing, or crop characteristics.
The farmer can finalize the exact quantity and price of a product they commit to supplying.
The farmer can see a list of products they need to deliver and their respective deadlines.
The store employee can create a new entry for a product, including its name, description, and initial characteristics.
The store employee can add an image to an existing product entry.
The store employee can specify how a product's quantity is measured.
The store employee can configure the allowable range for customer orders of a specific product.
The store employee can modify the information associated with a product in the catalog.
The store employee can find a customer's account in the system.
The store employee can open the ordering screen as if they were the selected customer.
The store employee can select items and specify amounts for a customer's order.
The store employee can finalize and send an order for a customer.
The store employee can see which products are expected from farmers.
The store employee can choose a specific delivery from the list to process.
The store employee can enter the actual amount of each product received from the farmer.
The store employee can finalize the receipt process for a delivery, updating its status in the system.
The store employee can access a list of all scheduled customer pickups for a given period.
The store employee can view the items and quantities for a particular customer's order.
The store employee can update the system to indicate that an order has been assembled and is ready.
The store employee can quickly locate a specific customer's order in the system.
The store employee can mark an order as 'picked up' in the system.
The system automatically deducts the order total from the customer's virtual wallet upon order confirmation.
The system automatically uses the customer's fair play score to determine precedence when allocating limited products.
The system automatically sends an SMS to the farmer if products are not delivered by 4 PM on the scheduled delivery day.
The system automatically cancels affected customer orders and re-credits their virtual wallet with a 20% bonus if a farmer fails to deliver by 8 PM.
The system automatically sends an SMS to the customer if they fail to pick up their order at the scheduled time.
The system automatically calculates and updates the customer's fair play score based on order, pickup, farmer delivery, and modification indicators.
